notes:
1. C. Rajagopalachari — Overview

  • Chakravarti Rajagopalachari was a lawyer, freedom fighter, Gandhian, administrator, writer and statesman.
  • He is popularly known as Rajaji.
  • He became:
  • Premier of Madras Presidency.
  • Governor of West Bengal.
  • Governor-General of India.
  • Union Home Minister.
  • Chief Minister of Madras State.
  • He later founded the Swatantra Party.
📌 Must-Memorise

C. Rajagopalachari → Rajaji → Vedaranyam + Governor-General + Swatantra Party

2. Birth

  • Rajaji was born on 10 December 1878.
  • He was born at Thorapalli near Hosur.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji → 10 December 1878 → Thorapalli

3. Present Location

  • Thorapalli is now in Krishnagiri district of Tamil Nadu.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Thorapalli → Rajaji Birthplace

4. Family

  • Rajaji was born into a Tamil-speaking family in the Salem region.
  • His father served in local judicial administration.

5. Education

  • Rajaji received his higher education in Bengaluru and Madras.
  • He later studied law.

6. Legal Career

  • Rajaji became a successful lawyer.
  • Salem became an important centre of his professional and early public life.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji → Lawyer → Salem

7. Salem

  • Rajaji practised law at Salem.
  • His early political and municipal career was also closely associated with Salem.

8. Salem Municipality

  • Rajaji served in the Salem municipal administration.
  • He became Chairman of the Salem Municipality during the late 1910s.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

Salem → Rajaji's Early Public Career

9. Municipal Reform

As municipal leader, he showed interest in:

  • Sanitation.
  • Civic administration.
  • Social reform.
  • Public welfare.

10. Social Reform

  • Rajaji opposed untouchability.
  • He supported reform of discriminatory social practices.

11. Entry into National Politics

  • Rajaji became increasingly active in the Indian National Congress during the early twentieth century.

12. Mahatma Gandhi

  • Rajaji became one of Mahatma Gandhi's closest political associates.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji → Major Gandhian Leader from Tamil Nadu

13. Gandhi's Confidence in Rajaji

  • Gandhi had very high confidence in Rajaji's judgement.
  • Rajaji was commonly described as one of Gandhi's closest intellectual and political associates.

14. Gandhian Politics

Rajaji supported:

  • Satyagraha.
  • Non-violence.
  • Swadeshi.
  • Khadi.
  • Constructive work.

15. Non-Cooperation Movement

  • Rajaji participated actively in the Non-Cooperation Movement launched in 1920.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji → Non-Cooperation Movement

16. Legal Profession and Nationalism

  • Like several nationalist lawyers, Rajaji moved away from a purely professional legal career and devoted himself increasingly to the freedom struggle.

17. Congress Organisation in South India

  • Rajaji helped strengthen Congress organisation in the Madras Presidency.

18. Tamil Nadu Congress Leadership

He emerged as one of the leading Congress figures in the Presidency along with leaders such as:

  • S. Satyamurti.
  • S. Srinivasa Iyengar.
  • C. Vijayaraghavachariar.
  • Later K. Kamarajar.

19. Vaikom Context

  • Rajaji supported campaigns against caste discrimination during the Gandhian period.
  • The broader South Indian anti-untouchability movement included the Vaikom Satyagraha of 1924–25.

20. Gandhi–Rajaji Relationship

  • Rajaji generally supported Gandhi's non-violent strategy.
  • At the same time, he was willing to differ from Gandhi and Congress colleagues on specific political questions.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Rajaji → Gandhian, But Independent Political Thinker

21. Simon Commission

  • Rajaji participated in the Congress-led opposition to colonial constitutional arrangements that excluded meaningful Indian representation.

22. Purna Swaraj Phase

  • Congress adopted Purna Swaraj at Lahore in 1929.
  • Rajaji supported the national struggle for complete independence.

23. Civil Disobedience Movement

  • Gandhi launched the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930.
  • Salt became its most powerful symbol.

24. Dandi March

  • Gandhi marched from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi in Gujarat.
  • He broke the salt law on 6 April 1930.

25. Tamil Nadu Parallel

  • Rajaji organised the principal Salt Satyagraha march in the Madras Presidency.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Tamil Nadu Salt Satyagraha → Rajaji

26. Vedaranyam Salt Satyagraha

  • Rajaji led the famous Vedaranyam Salt Satyagraha in April 1930.
📌 Must-Memorise

Vedaranyam Salt Satyagraha → Rajaji → 1930

27. Starting Point

  • The march began from Tiruchirappalli.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji Salt March → Tiruchirappalli to Vedaranyam

28. Start Date

  • Rajaji's march began on 13 April 1930.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Vedaranyam March Begins → 13 April 1930

29. Destination

  • The march proceeded toward Vedaranyam on the Tamil coast.

30. Vedaranyam

  • Vedaranyam is located in the Cauvery delta/coastal region of Tamil Nadu.
  • It became the principal Tamil symbol of the Salt Satyagraha.

31. Route

  • Rajaji and his volunteers passed through numerous towns and villages.
  • Public meetings were held along the route.

32. Objectives

The march sought to:

  • Defy the British salt monopoly.
  • Mobilise the public.
  • Spread Civil Disobedience.
  • Promote national unity.

33. Agasthiyampalli

  • Salt-law defiance connected with the Vedaranyam campaign took place near the coastal salt areas around Agasthiyampalli.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

Agasthiyampalli → Vedaranyam Salt Satyagraha

34. Salt Law Broken

  • Rajaji and his volunteers violated the colonial salt law at the end of April 1930.

35. Sardar Vedaratnam

  • Sardar A. Vedaratnam Pillai was an important local organiser of the Vedaranyam movement.
📌 Must-Memorise

Sardar Vedaratnam → Vedaranyam Salt Satyagraha

36. Local Support

  • Vedaratnam helped arrange:
  • Accommodation.
  • Supplies.
  • Local mobilisation.

37. Rukmini Lakshmipathi

  • Rukmini Lakshmipathi was an important Tamil woman nationalist associated with the Civil Disobedience and Salt Satyagraha period.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Rukmini Lakshmipathi → Salt Satyagraha / Congress

38. Women in Salt Satyagraha

  • Women participated in:
  • Processions.
  • Salt-law violation.
  • Picketing.
  • Boycott campaigns.

39. Arrest of Rajaji

  • Rajaji was arrested during the Vedaranyam Salt Satyagraha.
📌 Must-Memorise

Vedaranyam → Rajaji Arrested

40. Dandi vs Vedaranyam

Dandi:

  • Gujarat.
  • Gandhi.
  • 1930.

Vedaranyam:

  • Tamil Nadu.
  • Rajaji.
  • 1930.
⚠️ TNPSC Favourite Trap

Dandi → Gandhi

Vedaranyam → Rajaji

41. Historical Importance of Vedaranyam

  • It brought the Civil Disobedience Movement into the Tamil countryside on a large scale.
  • It is one of the most important events in Tamil Nadu's freedom-struggle history.

42. Rajaji and Gandhi–Irwin Phase

  • Rajaji remained within Congress leadership during the negotiations and reorganisation following the first Civil Disobedience phase.

43. Congress Working Committee

  • Rajaji served at different periods as an influential member of the Congress's central leadership.

44. Imprisonment

  • Rajaji underwent imprisonment for participation in the freedom struggle.

45. Constructive Programme

Rajaji supported Gandhian activities such as:

  • Khadi.
  • Village work.
  • Anti-untouchability.
  • Prohibition.

46. Prohibition

  • Rajaji became a strong advocate of prohibition.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji → Prohibition

47. Government of India Act 1935

  • The Act introduced provincial autonomy.
  • Provincial elections were held in 1937.

48. Congress Victory in Madras

  • Congress won a major victory in the 1937 election in the Madras Presidency.

49. Premier of Madras Presidency

  • Rajaji became Premier of the Madras Presidency in 1937.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji → Premier of Madras → 1937

50. Premier vs Chief Minister

  • Before independence, the head of the provincial ministry was commonly called Premier.
  • After the constitutional transition, the title Chief Minister became standard.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

1937 Rajaji → Premier of Madras Presidency

51. Rajaji Ministry

  • His ministry lasted from 1937 until 1939.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji's First Madras Ministry → 1937–1939

52. Provincial Autonomy

  • Rajaji's government functioned under the provincial-autonomy provisions of the Government of India Act 1935.

53. Prohibition Policy

  • His government expanded prohibition measures in parts of the Madras Presidency.

54. Sales Tax

  • The Madras Presidency under Rajaji became an important early adopter of a general sales-tax system.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

Rajaji Ministry → Early Sales Tax Administration

55. Temple Entry Reform

  • Rajaji's ministry supported legislation facilitating temple entry for communities historically excluded by caste.

56. Temple Entry Authorization

  • The Temple Entry Authorization and Indemnity legislation of 1939 became an important social-reform measure of the Madras Presidency.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Temple Entry Reform → Rajaji Ministry → 1939

57. Untouchability

  • Rajaji regarded removal of untouchability as an important Gandhian social objective.

58. Compulsory Hindi

  • Rajaji's government introduced compulsory teaching of Hindi in selected schools in the Madras Presidency.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Compulsory Hindi → Rajaji Ministry → 1937–39 Period

59. Anti-Hindi Agitation

  • The policy triggered a major anti-Hindi agitation in Tamil Nadu.
📌 Must-Memorise

First Major Anti-Hindi Agitation → Rajaji Ministry Period

60. Periyar

  • E.V. Ramasamy became one of the strongest leaders opposing compulsory Hindi.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Anti-Hindi Agitation → Periyar

61. Justice Party

  • Justice Party and Self-Respect Movement activists also opposed compulsory Hindi.

62. Nature of Opposition

Opponents argued that compulsory Hindi:

  • Threatened Tamil linguistic interests.
  • Imposed an unnecessary language burden.
  • Reflected cultural domination.

63. Rajaji's Position

  • Rajaji regarded Hindi learning as useful for wider communication in India.
  • His critics strongly rejected making it compulsory.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Language Policy → Major Rajaji–Dravidian Movement Conflict

64. Second World War

  • The Second World War began in September 1939.

65. India Declared at War

  • The British government declared India at war without consulting Indian elected representatives.

66. Congress Response

  • Congress demanded a clear declaration concerning Indian freedom.

67. Congress Ministries Resign

  • Congress provincial ministries resigned in 1939.
📌 Must-Memorise

Congress Ministries Resigned → 1939

68. Rajaji Resigns

  • Rajaji's Madras ministry resigned as part of this all-India Congress decision.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji Madras Ministry Ends → 1939

69. War Strategy Differences

  • Rajaji later differed from several Congress leaders over how India should respond to World War II.

70. Rajaji and World War II

  • Rajaji believed that the threat posed by fascism had to be taken seriously.
  • He became more willing than many Congress colleagues to consider conditional cooperation with Britain if Indian freedom was guaranteed.

71. Political Realism

  • Rajaji became known for proposing negotiated settlements even when they were unpopular within Congress.

72. Pakistan Question

  • Rajaji was among the earliest senior Congress leaders to argue that the Muslim League's Pakistan demand could not simply be ignored.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji → Early Congress Advocate of Negotiated Pakistan Settlement

73. Difference with Congress

  • This position placed Rajaji at odds with much of the Congress leadership during the early 1940s.

74. Quit India Movement

  • Congress launched Quit India in August 1942.
  • Rajaji did not support the Quit India strategy.
⚠️ TNPSC Favourite Trap

Rajaji → Did Not Support Quit India Movement

75. Reason for Difference

  • Rajaji feared that an immediate confrontation during World War II could weaken resistance to Axis powers.
  • He preferred a negotiated political settlement.

76. Rajaji and Congress

  • His differences over wartime strategy temporarily distanced him from mainstream Congress leadership.

77. C.R. Formula

  • Rajaji proposed a formula for resolving the Congress–Muslim League deadlock.
📌 Must-Memorise

C.R. Formula → C. Rajagopalachari

78. Year of C.R. Formula

  • The formula became particularly important in 1944.
📌 Must-Memorise

C.R. Formula → 1944

79. Purpose

The C.R. Formula attempted to:

  • Secure Muslim League support for Indian independence.
  • Find a negotiated solution to the Pakistan question.
  • Avoid continued political deadlock.

80. Core Principle

  • The proposal accepted the possibility of separation if the people of clearly defined Muslim-majority areas chose it through a plebiscite.

81. Plebiscite

  • A vote would be held after the end of the war in specified contiguous Muslim-majority districts.

82. Independence First

  • The Muslim League was expected to cooperate with Congress in securing independence and establishing an interim arrangement.

83. Partition by Consent

  • Separation would depend on the result of a plebiscite rather than automatic acceptance of the League's full territorial demand.

84. Common Matters

  • If partition occurred, agreements would be required regarding matters such as:
  • Defence.
  • Commerce.
  • Communications.

85. Gandhi's Use of Formula

  • Gandhi used Rajaji's proposal as an important basis for negotiations with Muhammad Ali Jinnah in 1944.
📌 Must-Memorise

C.R. Formula → Basis for Gandhi–Jinnah Talks

86. Gandhi–Jinnah Talks

  • Gandhi and Jinnah held discussions in Bombay in 1944.
📌 Must-Memorise

Gandhi–Jinnah Talks → 1944

87. Outcome

  • The talks failed to produce agreement.

88. Jinnah's Objections

  • Jinnah regarded the formula as insufficient because it did not fully accept the Muslim League's conception of Pakistan.

89. Historical Significance

  • The C.R. Formula showed Rajaji's willingness to acknowledge the possibility of Partition before many other senior Congress leaders did.

90. C.R. Formula — Exam Trap

C.R. Formula:

  • Rajaji.
  • 1944.
  • Congress–League settlement.
  • Plebiscite.
  • Gandhi–Jinnah negotiations.
📌 Must-Memorise

C.R. ≠ Cripps

C.R. → Rajagopalachari

91. Cripps Mission vs C.R. Formula

Cripps Mission:

  • British initiative.
  • 1942.
  • Stafford Cripps.

C.R. Formula:

  • Indian political proposal.
  • Rajaji.
  • 1944.
⚠️ TNPSC Favourite Trap

Do Not Confuse Cripps Proposal with C.R. Formula

92. Return to Congress Mainstream

  • Rajaji later returned to a central role in Congress and national politics.

93. Independence

  • India achieved independence on 15 August 1947.

94. Partition

  • British India was partitioned into India and Pakistan in 1947.
  • Rajaji's earlier warnings about the depth of the communal deadlock gained renewed attention.

95. Governor of West Bengal

  • Rajaji became Governor of West Bengal after independence.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji → Governor of West Bengal → 1947–48

96. Bengal Context

  • His governorship came during the difficult period following:
  • Partition.
  • Refugee movement.
  • Communal tensions.

97. Lord Mountbatten

  • Lord Mountbatten served as independent India's first Governor-General.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

First Governor-General of Independent India → Lord Mountbatten

98. Rajaji as Governor-General

  • Rajaji succeeded Lord Mountbatten as Governor-General in June 1948.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji → Governor-General → 1948

99. First Indian Governor-General

  • Rajaji became the first Indian to hold the office of Governor-General.
📌 Must-Memorise

First Indian Governor-General → C. Rajagopalachari

100. Only Indian Governor-General

  • Rajaji was also the only Indian to serve as Governor-General.
📌 Must-Memorise

Only Indian Governor-General → Rajaji

101. Last Governor-General

  • Rajaji became the last Governor-General of India.
📌 Must-Memorise

Last Governor-General of India → Rajaji

102. Tenure

  • Rajaji served as Governor-General from 1948 until India became a Republic on 26 January 1950.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji Governor-General → 1948–1950

103. End of Governor-General's Office

  • The office ended when India became a Republic on 26 January 1950.

104. President of India

  • Dr. Rajendra Prasad became the first President of India on 26 January 1950.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Last Governor-General → Rajaji

First President → Rajendra Prasad

105. Governor-General Sequence

Independent India:

  • Lord Mountbatten → First Governor-General.
  • C. Rajagopalachari → First and only Indian Governor-General; last Governor-General.
📌 Must-Memorise

Mountbatten → First

Rajaji → First Indian + Last

106. Union Cabinet

  • After his Governor-Generalship, Rajaji served in the Union government.

107. Sardar Patel

  • Vallabhbhai Patel was independent India's first Home Minister.
  • Rajaji later succeeded him in the Home Affairs portfolio after Patel's death.
📌 Must-Memorise

First Home Minister → Sardar Patel

Later Home Minister → Rajaji

108. Union Home Minister

  • Rajaji served as Union Home Minister during 1950–51.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji → Union Home Minister

109. Nehru and Rajaji

  • Rajaji and Jawaharlal Nehru were old Congress colleagues.
  • Their political and economic differences became increasingly significant after independence.

110. Madras Politics Again

  • Rajaji later returned to state politics.

111. Chief Minister of Madras State

  • Rajaji became Chief Minister of Madras State in 1952.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji → Madras Chief Minister → 1952

112. Tenure

  • He served as Chief Minister from 1952 to 1954.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji Madras CM → 1952–1954

113. Election Context

  • Rajaji did not enter the Chief Minister's office through a direct constituency victory in the 1952 Assembly election.
  • He entered the legislature through the upper house and formed the government in a politically fragmented Assembly.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

1952 Madras Politics → Coalition/Fragmented Legislature Context

114. Madras State

  • The state was still officially called Madras State.
  • It was renamed Tamil Nadu only in 1969.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Rajaji Was CM of Madras State, Not Officially "Tamil Nadu" at That Time

115. Prohibition

  • Rajaji continued to support prohibition during his later political career.

116. Education Policy

  • His second Madras administration introduced a controversial Modified Scheme of Elementary Education.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Rajaji → Modified Scheme of Elementary Education

117. Modified Elementary Education Scheme

  • The scheme reduced part of the school day and envisaged children spending additional time learning practical or occupational activities.

118. Critics' Interpretation

  • Opponents argued that the scheme would reinforce hereditary caste occupations.

119. "Kula Kalvi"

  • Critics popularly referred to it as the Kula Kalvi Thittam or hereditary education scheme.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Kula Kalvi Controversy → Rajaji Government

120. Periyar's Opposition

  • Periyar strongly opposed the scheme.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Periyar → Opposed Rajaji's Education Scheme

121. DMK Opposition

  • The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam also strongly opposed the policy.

122. Congress Opposition

  • Opposition also emerged within sections of the Congress organisation.

123. Kamarajar

  • K. Kamarajar eventually succeeded Rajaji as Chief Minister in 1954.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji → Kamarajar → Madras CM Transition, 1954

124. Resignation

  • Rajaji resigned as Chief Minister in 1954.

125. End of Education Scheme

  • The controversial education scheme was discontinued after the change in leadership.

126. Rajaji vs Kamarajar — Exam Link

Rajaji:

  • Madras CM → 1952–54.

Kamarajar:

  • Madras CM → 1954 onward.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

1954 → Rajaji to Kamarajar

127. Rajaji and Congress Economic Policy

  • Rajaji increasingly disagreed with the Congress's post-independence economic direction.

128. Nehruvian Planning

Nehru favoured:

  • Planning.
  • Large public sector.
  • Heavy industry.
  • Extensive state direction.

129. Rajaji's Economic View

Rajaji increasingly favoured:

  • Private enterprise.
  • Competition.
  • Agricultural interests.
  • Limited state control.

130. Opposition to Excessive State Control

  • Rajaji argued that excessive licensing and economic control could:
  • Reduce initiative.
  • Increase bureaucracy.
  • Encourage corruption.

131. Permit-Licence Raj

  • Rajaji became a prominent critic of the system later popularly described as the licence-permit system.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji → Critic of Licence-Permit Raj

132. Swatantra Party

  • Rajaji helped establish the Swatantra Party in 1959.
📌 Must-Memorise

Swatantra Party → 1959 → Rajaji

133. Co-Founders and Associates

Important leaders associated with its formation included:

  • C. Rajagopalachari.
  • N.G. Ranga.
  • Minoo Masani.
📌 Must-Memorise

Swatantra Party → Rajaji + N.G. Ranga + Minoo Masani

134. N.G. Ranga

  • N.G. Ranga was a prominent peasant leader.
  • He became an important figure in the Swatantra Party.

135. Minoo Masani

  • Minoo Masani was an important liberal political thinker and leader of the party.

136. Swatantra Party Ideology

The party criticised:

  • Centralised planning.
  • Excessive nationalisation.
  • State monopolies.
  • Licensing controls.

It supported:

  • Private enterprise.
  • Market competition.
  • Property rights.

137. Political Position

  • Swatantra Party represented an important non-socialist opposition to Congress economic policies.
📌 Must-Memorise

Swatantra → Market-Oriented Opposition to Congress Socialism

138. Agricultural Support

  • The party gained support from some:
  • Farmers.
  • Landholders.
  • Business groups.
  • Regional political elites.

139. Electoral Growth

  • Swatantra Party became a significant opposition party during the 1960s.

140. 1967 General Election

  • It emerged as the largest single opposition party in the Lok Sabha after the 1967 general election.
📌 Must-Memorise

Swatantra Party → Major Opposition Force → 1967

141. Rajaji and DMK

  • In the 1960s, Rajaji cooperated politically with parties opposed to Congress dominance, including the DMK in Tamil Nadu.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

Rajaji → Anti-Congress Alliances in 1960s

142. Anti-Congress Politics

  • Rajaji's later alliances reflected his view that one-party dominance should be checked by a strong opposition.

143. Democratic Opposition

  • He considered organised opposition essential to parliamentary democracy.

144. Rajaji and Hindi — Later Position

  • Rajaji's language position evolved over time.
  • Although his 1937 ministry had introduced compulsory Hindi instruction, he later opposed making Hindi the sole compulsory all-India official language at the expense of non-Hindi speakers.
⚠️ TNPSC Favourite

Rajaji's Language Position Changed Over Time

145. English as Link Language

  • In his later years, Rajaji supported continued use of English as a link language.

146. Tamil Nadu Language Politics

  • This later position brought him closer to anti-Hindi political forces in Tamil Nadu on certain issues.

147. Rajaji and Nuclear Weapons

  • In later life, Rajaji became an advocate of nuclear disarmament and world peace.

148. International Peace

  • He participated in campaigns urging major powers to halt nuclear testing.

149. Rajaji and United States

  • In the early 1960s, Rajaji travelled abroad as part of efforts connected with nuclear-disarmament advocacy.

150. Rajaji as Writer

  • Rajaji was a distinguished writer in both:
  • Tamil.
  • English.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji → Statesman + Tamil Writer

151. Epic Retellings

  • Rajaji produced highly popular retellings of:
  • Ramayana.
  • Mahabharata.

152. Chakravarthi Thirumagan

  • Rajaji's Tamil retelling of the Ramayana is known as Chakravarthi Thirumagan.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Chakravarthi Thirumagan → Rajaji → Ramayana

153. Sahitya Akademi Award

  • Rajaji received the Sahitya Akademi Award for Tamil for Chakravarthi Thirumagan in 1958.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji → Sahitya Akademi Award → 1958

154. Vyasar Virundhu

  • Rajaji wrote a popular Tamil rendering of the Mahabharata known as Vyasar Virundhu.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Vyasar Virundhu → Rajaji → Mahabharata

155. English Retellings

  • His English retellings of the Ramayana and Mahabharata also became widely read.

156. Simple Prose Style

  • Rajaji was known for clear, concise and accessible prose.

157. Religious and Ethical Writing

  • His literary works often emphasised:
  • Ethics.
  • Duty.
  • Moral choice.
  • Indian philosophical traditions.

158. Tamil Literature Contribution

  • Rajaji's writing helped present classical and epic traditions in modern, readable Tamil prose.

159. "Kurai Ondrum Illai"

  • Rajaji wrote the famous Tamil devotional song Kurai Ondrum Illai.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Kurai Ondrum Illai → C. Rajagopalachari

160. M.S. Subbulakshmi Connection

  • Kurai Ondrum Illai became especially famous through performances by M.S. Subbulakshmi.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

Rajaji → Kurai Ondrum Illai

M.S. Subbulakshmi → Famous Performance

161. Journalism and Political Commentary

  • Rajaji wrote extensively on:
  • Politics.
  • Economics.
  • Culture.
  • International affairs.

162. Swarajya

  • Rajaji became closely associated with the journal Swarajya.
  • It became an important platform for his later political and economic views.
📌 Must-Memorise

Swarajya → Rajaji's Later Political Thought

163. Intellectual Independence

  • Rajaji frequently took political positions that differed from prevailing Congress opinion.

164. Pragmatism

  • His political style was strongly associated with:
  • Negotiation.
  • Practical compromise.
  • Institutional politics.

165. Criticism

  • His willingness to compromise also made several of his proposals controversial.

166. Rajaji and Gandhi

Areas of agreement:

  • Non-violence.
  • Personal discipline.
  • Social reform.
  • Ethical politics.

Areas of occasional disagreement:

  • Wartime strategy.
  • Political settlements.
  • Practical policy choices.

167. Rajaji and Nehru

They differed especially over:

  • Economic planning.
  • Role of the state.
  • Private enterprise.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Nehru → Planning/Socialistic Pattern

Rajaji → Economic Liberalism/Swatantra

Their relationship involved major ideological conflict over:

  • Caste.
  • Religion.
  • Hindi.
  • Education policy.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Rajaji ↔ Periyar → Major Ideological Opponents

169. Rajaji and Kamarajar

  • Both were major Tamil Congress leaders.
  • Kamarajar succeeded Rajaji as Madras Chief Minister in 1954.

170. Rajaji and Satyamurti

  • Rajaji and S. Satyamurti represented two important streams within Tamil Congress politics.
  • They sometimes differed over organisational and electoral strategy.

171. Rajaji and Bharathiar

  • Both belonged to Tamil Nadu's wider nationalist intellectual tradition, though Bharathiar's principal nationalist activity predated Rajaji's later political prominence.

172. Bharat Ratna

  • Rajaji received the Bharat Ratna in 1954.
📌 Must-Memorise

Rajaji → Bharat Ratna → 1954

173. First Bharat Ratna Awardees

The first Bharat Ratna awards in 1954 went to:

  • C. Rajagopalachari.
  • Dr. S. Radhakrishnan.
  • C.V. Raman.
📌 Must-Memorise

1954 Bharat Ratna → Rajaji + Radhakrishnan + C.V. Raman

174. Rajaji's Historical Firsts

Rajaji was:
